lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: So you've finally come down to join us, Polystratus — and what, a good ninety-something years on the books?
lines.description: wry welcome, gently needling an old acquaintance

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Ninety-eight, Simylus.
lines.description: cheerful precision, proud of the number

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: And how did you manage those last thirty after me? I died when you were pushing seventy.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: I had a wonderful time. I know that'll sound improbable to you.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Improbable is the word. Old, frail, no children — and you're telling me you enjoyed yourself?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: I could do whatever I liked. There were still plenty of pretty boys around, and the most exquisite women, and perfumes, and vintage wine, and a table that would have embarrassed a Sicilian.
lines.description: luxuriant reminiscence, amused by his own excess

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: This is news. I knew you as a notorious tightwad.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: My dear fellow, the good things flowed in from other people. From dawn onward there'd be a crowd at my door, and then gifts of every kind would come pouring in — the finest from every corner of the earth.
lines.description: relishing the reveal, genial and expansive

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: What, did you become a tyrant after I died, Polystratus?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: No. I had lovers. Thousands of them.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: [laughs] Lovers. You. At that age. With four teeth in your head.
lines.description: laughing, then puncturing each phrase with delight

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: By Zeus, yes — the best men in the city. Old, bald — as you can see — bleary-eyed, dribbling at the nose, and they were absolutely thrilled to wait on me. The luckiest man in town was whichever one I deigned to glance at.
lines.description: gleefully shameless, savoring every degrading detail

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Don't tell me you ferried Aphrodite across from Chios like Phaon, and she granted your prayer to be young and beautiful and desirable all over again?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: No. I was exactly as you see me — and much sought after.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: You're talking in riddles.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Oh come now — it's the most obvious thing in the world. The standard, well-known passion for childless rich old men.
lines.description: matter-of-fact reveal, dry and faintly patronizing

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: [laughs] Ah. Now I understand your beauty, my dear fellow. Pure gift of golden Aphrodite.

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Still, Simylus, I got a great deal out of my lovers. They practically worshipped me. I played hard to get — used to shut the door on some of them now and then — and they'd compete with each other, outbidding one another for my favour.
lines.description: cheerful manipulator, proud of a well-run con

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: And in the end — what did you decide about the estate?
lines.description: leaning in, eager for the final turn

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Officially, I told each of them in turn that I was leaving him as heir. Each one believed it, and redoubled his flattery. But I had the real will tucked away somewhere else — and that's the one I left behind. The lot of them could go hang.
lines.description: genial ruthlessness, delighted with the mechanism

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: So who did the real will name? Some relative, presumably?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Good lord, no. A pretty Phrygian boy I'd just bought.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: How old, roughly?

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: About twenty.

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Ah. Now I see what services he'd been rendering.
lines.description: dry comprehension, sly but not broad

lines.speaker: Polystratus
lines.text: Well — he was a great deal more deserving than they were, barbarian and wretch though he was. The cream of society is now waiting on him. So he inherited from me, and he's currently counted among the nobility — chin shaved smooth, accent thick as ever — and they're calling him better-born than Codrus, handsomer than Nireus, and shrewder than Odysseus.
lines.description: pleased storyteller, rising amusement at social inversion

lines.speaker: Simylus
lines.text: Suits me. Let him command the armies of Greece, for all I care — so long as that crowd of theirs gets nothing.
